summary: Team Misson KAJM developed the Earth System Trend Detective, a professional, single-screen dashboard web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.Tracking Earth science variables comes with a major puzzle: the exact same global process can cause opposite trends in different regions. To solve this, our tool integrates official data sources—including NASA Giovanni, AppEEARS, SWOT, CDO, and CSA Radarsat—allowing users to select environmental phenomena, visualize de-seasonalized time-series graphs, and run rigorous statistical significance tests ($p$-values) to verify real climate trends versus weather noise.The app features a compact 2x2 mission-control grid with a Light/Dark mode toggle, regional hotspot trackers, ecosystem impact assessments, a detective Q&A section, and direct data portal links. It bridges complex satellite data with student accessibility, turning raw archives into actionable environmental insights.
details:
What It Does & How It Works The Earth System Trend Detective, created by Team Misson KAJM, is an interactive, single-screen environmental dashboard designed to help users explore and verify long-term climate and Earth science trends. Users choose an environmental phenomenon—such as Arctic Ice Melt, Tropical Deforestation, Global Surface Water Shifts, Drought Contrasts, or Coastal Sea Ice Change—from a dropdown menu and click Analyze Overview. The tool immediately populates a compact 2x2 mission-control grid displaying statistical significance metrics ($p$-values, rate of change, and cumulative shifts), a multi-year time-series line graph, regional hotspot coordinates explaining opposite regional trends, and ecosystem impact and mitigation strategies.

Benefits & Intended Impact Raw satellite archives can be overwhelming for students, educators, and early researchers. Our tool bridges the gap between complex Earth observation datasets and everyday accessibility. By combining visual trend tracking with statistical significance testing, it helps users distinguish true environmental shifts from short-term weather fluctuations and understand how a single global driver can produce opposite trends in different regions.

Tools, Languages & Data Sources Used

  • Frontend & Coding Languages: Built using lightweight, clean HTML5, CSS3 (CSS Grid and custom theme variables), and JavaScript.
  • Data Visualization: Powered by Chart.js for responsive, dynamic time-series plotting.
  • Official Data Portals & Resources: Anchored in NASA and international partner missions, including NASA Giovanni, NASA AppEEARS, SWOT Mission, NOAA CDO Hydrology, KNMI Climate Explorer, and CSA Radarsat Constellation Mission (RCM).

Creativity & Design Considerations To maximize clarity and eliminate endless vertical scrolling during live evaluations, our team engineered a clutter-free 2x2 grid architecture where all core insights appear in a single glance. We also integrated an on-demand Analyze Overview trigger, a top-level Light Mode / Dark Mode switcher that dynamically adapts chart axes and gridlines for comfortable day or night viewing, a 5-part Detective Q&A guide, and direct portal links for deeper exploration.
